posts.content_md:
Sounds like rose scented anti-freeze? =')

- Propylene-Glycol (editable anti-freeze):

[http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Propylene_glycol](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Propylene_glycol)

Glycerin (a solvent better than water or alcohol. Tends to suck the water out of the air to roughly become 80% glycerin, 20% water):

[http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glycerin](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glycerin)

Sodium benzoate (I think this is what you meant, right? It's a food preservative):

[http://www.encyclopedia.com/html/s1/sodiumbe.asp](http://www.encyclopedia.com/html/s1/sodiumbe.asp)

Water (aka, stuff that hits you in the shower. Stuff that you swill down as a chaser after good vodka. Stuff that you get annoyed with when it comes down in quantity from the sky unexpectedly):

[http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water)

(Actually, take a look at this link. This is what information evolution on a well visited wiki gives you. Great balance of common experience and technnical. Lots of links.)

Artificial rose fragrance (i.e., stuff that smells nice):

[http://www.joelssalon.com/fragranc.htm](http://www.joelssalon.com/fragranc.htm) (caution on the image to the right... *barf*)
So, what are you hinting at? Is this the secret additive for DCG? What wouldn't freeze, smell nice, and not 'go bad' after a while? Water and glycerin would make it feel nice on the skin. Hummmm..

But, 80% Propylene-Glycol? That's a lot. The primary use of the substance is there, to be sure.

-Phil
